name: Nanotube deorbit tether
subtitle: a fuel-free tether that drags dead satellites down

effects.effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal

effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal
how: Dead satellites linger in orbit for decades, raising the risk of collisions, and carrying fuel to bring them down eats into payload. At end of life a satellite unrolls a kilometres-long nanotube tape; moving through the Earth's magnetic field drives a current along it, and the field pushes back on that current, braking the satellite until it burns up within months.
obstacle: Long tethers get cut by tiny debris, and unrolling them reliably has failed on past missions.
why: Japan's 2017 tether test failed to deploy; no satellite has been brought down this way.
real: Carbon nanotube yarn and tape tethers for electrodynamic-tether deorbit kits are in development and were planned for CubeSats, but no confirmed in-orbit deorbit with a nanotube tether was found (TEPCE used a non-CNT tether).
